beats.narration_text: Namaste. I'm Siddhesh Nikam, and this is the pitch for my final project. Lots of tools will answer a data question. My question is different. Can I prove the answer is right?

show.event: 'answer' is corrected to 'prove its answers to'

props.text:
Can Claude answer
my campaign questions?

beats.motion_claim: The writer types 'can Claude answer my campaign questions' and corrects it to proving the answers.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. ROAS, return on ad spend: revenue divided by what the ads cost. A prompt contract: the fixed rules I give Claude about what it may write, and in what form. And a test set: questions whose right answers I work out by hand, before Claude sees them.

terms.meaning: Return On Ad Spend: sales divided by the ad budget
fixed rules that limit what Claude will write
questions I solve by hand first: the key

beats.narration_text: One sentence. CheckedSQL will let a marketing analyst ask a campaign question in plain English, have Claude write the S Q L, run it on the data, and show the answer beside the query, scored against an answer key.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a GitHub repository, and part of it already runs. On October twenty-fourth, with Claude's help, I built the synthetic dataset, ten test questions with an answer key, and the checker. Still to come: the prompt contract, the Claude step, and the evaluation log.

beats.narration_text: Why would anyone care? The first alternative is a fixed dashboard, like the Tableau dashboard in my marketing campaign project, which I made with AI help. It answers the questions planned in advance. A new question means building a new view.

shot.visual_intent: A dashboard with three coloured channel bars grows; a new question card slides toward it and bounces back.
shot.motion_claim: A dashboard with three coloured channel bars grows; a new question card slides toward it and bounces back.

beats.narration_text: The second is a general chat assistant. On October twenty-fourth, I gave ChatGPT my campaign data and asked which channel had the highest ROAS. It answered Search, which is right. But there is no fixed test set, so no record of how often it is right on my questions, or which ones it gets wrong. CheckedSQL runs every answer, shows its query, and scores it.

shot.visual_intent: My real ChatGPT answer (cropped screenshot, Oct 24) framed; an arrow to 'Search'; my answer-key card agrees with a check; then a row of ten questions with only one answered: one answer is not a record.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager for a data analyst role. In the first sixty seconds, they open the README, run one command, python three checker dot P Y, and see a score table. That command already works today.

beats.narration_text: What will it prove? That I can get marketing metrics right and check them against an answer key. And three course skills: a prompt contract, verification against known answers, and evaluation I can repeat. Verification and evaluation now have real evidence: the checker and its score table. The contract is next.

beats.narration_text: What's out: it will never change the database. The checker already refuses anything but a single read-only SELECT. One schema, no dashboards, and no real company data: these twenty-four rows are synthetic.

beats.narration_text: What came first was the baseline, before any Claude call: ten questions, an answer key worked out from the totals, and baseline S Q L drafted with Claude. The checker printed ten out of ten. Then I added two deliberately wrong queries that average ROAS row by row. The checker failed both.

show.event: lens stops on the trap row

beats.narration_text: What could sink it? An answer that looks right but isn't. These are Email's eight real rows. Four of them spend almost nothing and return fourteen to twenty times that. Average the row ratios, and Email's ROAS comes out at nine point seven five.

shot.visual_intent: Eight blue bars, one per Email row, height = that row's ROAS; four tower; a dashed line lands at 9.75, labelled row average.
shot.motion_claim: Eight blue bars, one per Email row, height = that row's ROAS; four tower; a dashed line lands at 9.75, labelled row average.

beats.narration_text: Divide total revenue by total spend instead, and Email is two point two nine. The best channel is Search, not Email. Both numbers look plausible. My fix: the metric definition goes in the prompt contract, and the test set has ratio questions, so this mistake gets caught, as it just was.

shot.visual_intent: The 9.75 ghost bar is crossed out; three channel bars at their true ROAS (Email 2.29, Search 3.98, Social 1.05); a check lands on Search.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? Mostly to learn. My earlier marketing campaign repository was built with a lot of AI help, so it shows the domain I care about, metrics like click-through rate and return on ad spend, more than it proves I can code alone. New to me: writing and checking S Q L myself, calling Claude from Python, prompt contracts, and evaluation. This project is how I'll prove those.

beats.narration_text: So, what exists today: my two earlier repositories, this film, and the first piece of CheckedSQL: the dataset, the questions, the answer key, and the checker. What will exist: the prompt contract, the Claude step, thirty questions, and the evaluation log. What I don't know yet is whether thirty is enough. I'll find out by watching whether new questions keep finding new kinds of failure.
